alternatives.name: DuckDB
alternatives.why_not_default: Selected. Remaining evidence gaps: (a) the broad-universe collection uses the provider's default as-of, 'provider default (request date)' (broad-universe/receipt.json line 90), so it is not a historical as-known snapshot; (b) the receipt says corporate-action coverage is thin before 2020 and the provider asset list under-enumerates delisted names (line 334); (c) 71.138 s is one elapsed time for one run, not a comparative throughput or concurrency measurement; (d) the DECIMAL(38,12) roundtrip used artificial fixtures, and the earlier live SEC acquisition returned http_403 (financial-data/receipt.json). The packet card's limitation that DuckDB 'proves neither market-data ingestion' is superseded by the later broad-universe receipt (generated_at 2026-09-21T23:55:30Z), which is outside the packet's c4 evidence_refs.

alternatives.name: Pandera
alternatives.why_not_default: Pandera has a retained fail-closed schema gate (data/promotion_gate.py lines 148-180 and 232-273), but it has run only on synthetic CSV fixtures (data/README.md lines 70-73). fixtures/good-gate-result.json records pass with 12 checks and row_count 4. fixtures/bad-gate-result.json records fail on valid_trading_session, volume_integral_non_negative, observed_at_not_future, high_ge_max_open_close and unique_symbol_session, with row_count 4. Both record pandera 0.33.1. The packet's evidence_refs list the upstream README only, and the gate's duckdb:// input path is source-only because duckdb is not in the gate venv (promotion_gate.py lines 13-16). Fail-closed rejection on real data in this layer is demonstrated by DuckDB SQL instead: coverage.py lines 484-502 and eligibility_gates over 24195741 candidate rows (broad-universe/receipt.json lines 1097-1099). Pandera becomes a co-winner if the gate runs fail-closed on a real DuckDB-produced snapshot.

alternatives.name: data-arrow
alternatives.why_not_default: pyarrow 25.0.1 appears only as a version field in the gate results. The gate read CSV fixtures, not Parquet (data/README.md lines 70-73). DuckDB wrote and reread the retained Parquet itself (summarize_backtest.py lines 25-26; coverage.py lines 521-523). I found no retained Arrow-specific check of precision or time-unit roundtrip, which the card's own limitation requires. The upstream README was not opened.

alternatives.name: data-dlt
alternatives.why_not_default: The only packet evidence is the upstream README URL, which was not opened. No local extraction or loading into DuckDB is retained; the retained broad-universe ingest uses project-owned collection and coverage code. The card says watermark-only extraction can miss late revisions and that schema inference is not a financial data-quality contract.

alternatives.name: data-iceberg
alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. No catalog, append, multi-writer or time-travel execution is retained. The packet's existing_overturn_when adds a lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it. The only measurement retained is one DuckDB elapsed time (71.138 s), with no comparison.

alternatives.name: ray-serve
alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. The card says no distributed performance or failover acceptance was performed. The largest retained workload, 24195741 bars evaluated in DuckDB in 71.138 s in a single run (broad-universe/receipt.json lines 1072-1086), shows no demonstrated need for distributed compute. This is untested, not failed.

alternatives.name: QuestDB
alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. The card says the catalog did not install or start a server. Adding a server requires local throughput/concurrency measurements (packet existing_overturn_when), and none are retained. Dedup/upsert can overwrite corrections.

alternatives.name: ClickHouse
alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. The card says the local SQL command is prospective, with no server, throughput or reliability evidence. The packet marks the pin v26.8.7.19-lts as behind upstream v26.9.2.8-stable. Eventual merges must not be treated as an immutable revision ledger.

alternatives.name: foundation-toon
alternatives.why_not_default: Native CLI execution exists, but for serialization rather than storage/compute. toon-encode and toon-decode both exited 0, with toon_roundtrip_equal true, in evidence/receipts/portable-cli-artifacts.json. component-history.json says native_claude and native_codex use is 'not independently demonstrated'. A nested fixture grew from 69 to 94 tokens. TOON serializes model context; it is not an analytical snapshot store.

alternatives.name: data-feast
alternatives.why_not_default: Source review only; the README URL was not opened. No feature-store execution is retained. The card says event-time point-in-time retrieval does not exclude late corrections, and that materialization freshness and skew need separate operational evidence.

alternatives.name: bytebase/dbhub
alternatives.why_not_default: Not adopted, with empty packet evidence_refs and card_limitations. Its note makes it conditional on a curated research database, a read-only principal and max_rows enforcement, and none of these is retained. It is an access layer, not storage or compute.

limits: I could not open the upstream GitHub README URLs for c1-c8 and c11 (no network or command access). The dispositions for candidates backed only by source review therefore rest on the packet card text.

I read only part of broad-universe/receipt.json (lines 1-100, 300-339, 1060-1109), read identity-readiness/native-receipt.json by grep only, and did not open daily.parquet, events.parquet or the ledger. I ran no tests or commands. All counts, timings and hashes are copied from retained receipts, not observed now.

The DuckDB real-data evidence (the broad-universe, catalyst-dataset and identity-readiness receipts) and the Pandera evidence are outside the packet's own evidence_refs. I found them through the revision-round refuter findings and scoped reads.

Revision changes: I dropped the claim that the Parquet fed a later workflow, because the Dagu step rebuilt a byte-identical Parquet (prepare-evidence.yaml lines 9-11). I corrected the gaps on market-data ingest, scale and corporate actions against broad-universe/receipt.json. I removed c8 from the winners so that the native_proven class holds for the whole winner set. I qualified the claim that DuckDB was the only candidate with native execution, and split overturn check (1) by environment with a zero-skip requirement.

The typesafe-ai skill was loaded from <host-path>/SKILL.md (injected at invocation). The coordinator supplied no TypeSafe inference results and I made none, so every judgment here is my own source review. The refuter findings were treated as leads and checked against the original files. The model is the packet-fixed opus/high; the client reports claude-opus-5-5[1m].
open_gaps: Historical as-known availability of market data is not established. The broad-universe collection uses 'asof': 'provider default (request date)' (broad-universe/receipt.json line 90). The only retained rejection of records not yet available at the as-of date is on SEC metadata: catalyst-dataset/native-receipt.json line 87 records 0 eligible headers as of 2020-03-03.

Corporate-action coverage is incomplete. The receipt says coverage 'is thin before 2020, so names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained action remain undiscoverable', and that the provider asset list under-enumerates delisted names (broad-universe/receipt.json line 334). Rename-pair de-duplication is implemented (coverage.py lines 484-493), but full adjustment reconciliation is not; the packet limitations cite missing dividend currency.

No comparative throughput or concurrency measurement exists. The only figure is one DuckDB elapsed time, 71.138 s (broad-universe/receipt.json line 1073), so the server, lake and distributed candidates (c2, c3, c5, c6) remain untested, not failed.

The Pandera gate has run only on 4-row synthetic CSV fixtures. Its duckdb:// input path is untested source code (promotion_gate.py lines 13-16), and it does not check corporate actions, as-known availability or provider completeness.
No retained check is dedicated to Arrow/Parquet precision or time-unit roundtrip under pyarrow.
Licensing and redistribution terms for the SIP feed are not established by the evidence I read. The receipt states 'real entitled provider data' but retains no rights terms.

arms: DuckDB 1.5.5 + Pandera 0.33.1 gate on the same real snapshot
overturn_protocol.metric: On one frozen, representative real snapshot, measure five things: exact DECIMAL/timestamp roundtrip equality; seeded-defect rejection that fails closed with no silent pass; a byte-identical Parquet hash on rebuild; local query latency/concurrency at the required universe size; and zero skipped tests in each pinned environment.

overturn_when: Any of three results would change this verdict. (1) The DuckDB checks stop passing with zero skips when each suite runs in its own pinned environment: run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_financial_data` with the research interpreter where duckdb is importable (skipUnless at tests/test_financial_data.py lines 229 and 246), and run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_promotion_gate` with the gate venv present (skipUnless at tests/test_promotion_gate.py line 90). A skip-only pass does not count. (2) Rerunning blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/coverage.py on the retained ledger fails to reproduce the recorded row totals (24195741 rows in contract) or does not fail closed on duplicate (symbol, session_date) rows. (3) An executed, frozen comparison on a representative real snapshot, including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, shows that ClickHouse, QuestDB or Iceberg/PyIceberg beats DuckDB. The comparison would measure exact DECIMAL/timestamp roundtrip, seeded-defect rejection, byte-identical snapshot rebuilds, and local throughput/concurrency at the required universe size. Pandera (c8) becomes a co-winner when blueprints/us-equities/data/promotion_gate.py runs fail-closed on a real DuckDB-produced snapshot with seeded defects.
why_selected:
c4 DuckDB is the only candidate in the storage/compute role with retained native execution. c10 TOON also has native CLI execution, but its role is serialization of model context. My own source review found four DuckDB receipts.
(1) blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/receipt.json records real entitled provider data (line 6: 'measured on real entitled provider data (read-only GETs)'). The plan uses feed 'sip', timeframe 1Day, 2016-01-01 to 2026-09-18 and 15418 symbols (lines 72-90). It collected 24310292 raw bars in 2554 pages, and the csv and ledger totals match (lines 22-57). The page sha256 re-verification shows 5108/5108 verified and 0 mismatches (lines 65-71). In broad-universe/coverage.py, DuckDB fails closed when the corporate-action ledger is incomplete or no rename pair loads (lines 484-493) and when duplicate (symbol, session_date) rows exist (lines 497-502). It then writes ZSTD Parquet and rereads the row count (lines 521-523). The evaluation ran duckdb_version 1.5.5 with elapsed_s 71.138, produced an events.parquet of 3532983 rows, used 24195741 bars and recorded 0 off-calendar rows. The eligibility gates covered 24195741 candidate rows (receipt lines 1070-1099).
(2) blueprints/us-equities/data/receipt.json (native_cli_e2e) records DuckDB (duckdb==1.5.5, workers/requirements.txt line 4) projecting 6 native LEAN simulated order events to DECIMAL(20,8), writing ZSTD Parquet and rereading it (summarize_backtest.py lines 19-28). The result was 3 distinct orders, 3 filled and 3 submitted, with parquet_sha256 48ec550a.... The Dagu order_table step (research-runtime/prepare-evidence.yaml lines 9-11) re-ran summarize_backtest.py on a fresh LEAN order-events file. It produced the same parquet_sha256 (research-runtime/receipt.json line 53), which shows a byte-identical rebuild, not the Parquet being passed downstream.
(3) catalyst-dataset/native-receipt.json line 89 records repeat_parquet_bytes_identical true. Line 87 shows historical as_of 2020-03-03 returning 0 eligible headers, so DuckDB rejected records not yet available at that date.
(4) financial-data/receipt.json offline_verification records an exact DECIMAL(38,12) roundtrip, but on artificial fixtures only.
Pandera (c8) is not a co-winner. Its only retained runs are on 4-row synthetic CSVs, and the real-data rejection evidence in this layer is DuckDB's.
